item.title: Kurobe Dam: Japan's Tallest Dam and Its Dramatic Discharge — Guide
item.description: Kurobe Dam, Japan’s tallest dam at 186 metres, was built through one of the country’s most demanding postwar construction projects, driving a tunnel through unstable, high-pressure rock to reach the remote gorge site. Today the dam is best known for its dramatic summer water discharge, when huge volumes of water are released down the dam face, often accompanied by a visible rainbow in the spray, set against a backdrop of Northern Japan Alps peaks reached as part of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.
